item.title: Ogun to convert 6,000 Amotekun, So-Safe personnel to state police — Abiodun
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has said the state is ready for the establishment of its own police force, disclosing that more than 6,000 personnel of the Ogun State Security Network, known as Amotekun, and the So-Safe Corps are available to provide the manpower for the proposed outfit. Abiodun said his administration had laid a solid foundation for state policing through the establishment of community-based security structures, noting that the existing personnel and operational experience of the two outfits would facilitate the transition. The governor spoke at the 50th anniversary celebration of Ereke Day in Ikenne, Ikenne Local Government Area of the state, where he described the Ogun State House of Assembly’s approval of the establishment of state police as a significant step towards strengthening security and protecting lives and property. Abiodun, who chairs the Nigeria Governors’ Forum Committee on State Police Creation and represents President Bola Tinubu on the committee, expressed confidence in the state’s readiness to implement the initiative. He said: “I am the Chairman of the Governors’ Forum on State Police Creation and the representative of the President in the Governors’ Forum on State Police Creation. I am proud to announce that the Ogun State House of Assembly has approved the creation of state police. “Between Amotekun and So-Safe Corps, we have over 6,000 personnel. We are ready for the Ogun State Police Command, and that will make the difference in protecting the lives and property of our people.” The governor stressed that security was essential to economic prosperity, investment and sustainable development, adding that meaningful progress could only be achieved in an atmosphere of peace and stability. He called for sustained collaboration between communities and security agencies to ensure the safety of residents, businesses and investors across the state. In a related development, Abiodun directed the immediate reconstruction of the Delabo-Ikenne Road, assuring residents that the project would improve accessibility, enhance connectivity and stimulate economic activities in the community. Speaking on the golden jubilee of Ereke Day, the governor described the 50-year celebration as a significant milestone reflecting the unity, common heritage and shared aspirations of the people of Ikenne. “Fifty years is very remarkable in the tradition and history of any people. It speaks to a united and common heritage, shared values and a collective determination to build a better future,” he said. He commended traditional rulers and the Ikenne Traditional Council of Chiefs for their leadership and commitment to preserving the community’s cultural identity while promoting development. item.title: Enugu pensioners recount past ordeals as Mbah pays 26-year gratuity arrears
item.description: …Pensioners hail governor as promise keeper . ..Mbah: No retiree should go to bed hungry Enugu State pensioners under the auspices of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners (NUP) have hailed Governor Peter Mbah for keeping his campaign promise to clear legacy arrears, describing their decades of disappointment after serving their fatherland as a harrowing experience. The pensioners spoke as retirees started receiving their gratuities dating back to the year 2000, with some also extending to the military era, saying the development had restored life to their bodies. The Chairman, Enugu State chapter of NUP, Ikechukwu Ekere, confirmed the development at the weekend, describing it as “an emotional moment for pensioners, many of whom had long given up hope of receiving their gratuities in their lifetime.” “Yes, I can confirm to you that our members have started receiving the alerts. Governor Mbah is a promise keeper; he has done it again and we can’t thank him enough,” he said. In the same vein, the Caretaker Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Pensioners, Local Government Staff Pensions Board Branch, Kenneth Ugwueze, told journalists that the development had restored hope and joy in many homes, saying that Mbah had, once again, proven himself as a leader who could be trusted. “You know what it means for a governor to pay debts incurred by many governors before him? It takes a large quantity of milk of human kindness. We are happy to see a day like this in our lifetime. We will continue to pray for him. “We are also grateful and happy with the new dimensions brought in by our governor in pension administration, especially in the local government system. “Before now, local government workers and primary school teachers who retired had to wait for two years before receiving their pensions. But since the conclusion of the verification exercise in July 2024, no pensioner in the local government system has been denied pension. We have been receiving our pensions as and when due. “Now that our people have started receiving alerts for their gratuity, it is a thing of joy,” he said. Some beneficiaries of the ongoing payments also expressed gratitude to the governor, describing the development as a rekindling of hope after years and devades of waiting. They said previous governments had not paid them even in the days of excess crude revenues. Mr. Luke Obi Ezea, who retired in 2014, said he had since resigned himself to fate and put everything in the hands of God. “I put in 35 years in service. Already, I had put everything in the hands of God because previous governors had made promises, but to no avail. They were just empty promises at the end of their eight years. But Peter Mbah is an action governor and keeps his word,” he stated. item.title: Governorship Debate: Why many Lagos residents remain poor – GRV explains
item.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate in Lagos State, Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, has accused successive state governments of prioritising elite interests over the welfare of ordinary residents. Rhodes-Vivour, popularly known as GRV, made the allegation during the Lagos governorship debate organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium held in Lagos on Sunday, where he outlined his plans to address the state’s challenges. He said his manifesto was designed to put residents first, adding that his administration would introduce practical solutions to problems including waste management, traffic congestion, healthcare and housing. “My manifesto has always stood with the people, putting the interest of the people first. I have that track record. We’re bringing solution thinking to the problems of Lagos State, waste management, traffic, healthcare, housing,” he said. The ADC candidate criticised the Lagos government over what he described as decades of policies focused on wealthy neighbourhoods and the elite, particularly in housing development. He cited the government’s approach to communities such as Makoko, accusing the authorities of celebrating the state’s development while pushing out residents from their communities. Rhodes-Vivour also questioned the impact of Lagos State’s internally generated revenue (IGR), arguing that the figures often celebrated by the government did not reflect the economic realities of ordinary residents. “Lagos government, in the last 20 years has its focus on elite policies, eyebrow areas for housing. That’s why on paper, Lagos celebrates a high IGR, but on ground, people are not feeling it. We would focus on people, our policies are tailored towards that.” He promised that an ADC-led administration would prioritise policies that directly address residents’ needs, reiterating his commitment to delivering 100,000 housing units. The debate was organised by the Nigeria Debate Consortium, comprising Channels Television, TVC News, The PUNCH, TheCable and Vanguard. Other major contenders at the debate include Lagos Deputy Governor and All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Obafemi Hamzat; Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate, Funso Doherty; and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Deji Doherty. item.title: Ogun police rescue 10 kidnap victims, kill suspect
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Ogun State Police Command has rescued 10 passengers abducted by suspected kidnappers at Orita Fufu, Awa-Ijebu, in Ijebu North-East Local Government Area of the state, following security operations and intelligence-led efforts. The victims, who were abducted from a commercial bus on November 3, 2026, regained their freedom unharmed at about 8:30 p.m. on Saturday, November 7. In a statement issued on Sunday, the Police Public Relations Officer of the command, DSP Oluseyi Babasayi, said the rescue was followed by an operation targeting the suspected kidnappers’ hideout along the Ibadan-Ijebu Ode Road. According to the statement, operatives of the Anti-Kidnapping Unit stormed the hideout at about 1 a.m. on Sunday, triggering a gun battle with the suspected criminals. One suspected kidnapper was neutralised during the encounter, while other members of the gang reportedly escaped with suspected gunshot wounds. The police said an AK-47 rifle, 20 rounds of ammunition, ₦1,376,800 in cash and a mobile phone were recovered during the operation. The command said it had intensified efforts to track down and arrest the fleeing suspects, adding that it remained committed to tackling kidnapping and other violent crimes in the state. It urged members of the public to remain vigilant and promptly report anyone seen with suspicious gunshot wounds to the nearest police station or through established police communication channels. The police also appealed for public cooperation, noting that information from residents could assist security operatives in locating the fleeing suspects and bringing them to justice. item.title: ADC crisis: Aregbesola appeals court judgment
item.description: Rauf Aregbesola, National Secretary of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has appealed the Federal High Court judgment nullifying the emergence of the David Mark-led leadership of the party. In a notice of appeal filed on Friday through his lawyer, Mohammed Sheriff, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), Aregbesola asked the Court of Appeal to set aside the judgment delivered by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court, Abuja, on the grounds that the court lacked jurisdiction to entertain the suit. Aregbesola listed Nafiu Gombe, the ADC, Mark, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and Ralph Nwosu as the first to fifth respondents, respectively. He urged the appellate court to overturn the lower court’s decision to assume jurisdiction over claims concerning his emergence as national secretary and the validity of resolutions reached at the party’s 99th National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting. The former Osun State governor also challenged the declaration that Gombe’s four-year tenure remained subsisting and that he was entitled to oversee the affairs of the party. Aregbesola further asked that, should the Court of Appeal uphold the lower court’s jurisdiction but find that a retrial is necessary, the affected claims be returned to the Federal High Court for hearing before another judge. In five grounds of appeal, Sheriff argued that Justice Lifu erred in law by holding that the challenge to INEC’s statutory oversight empowered the lower court to determine competing claims to the ADC leadership arising from the 99th NEC meeting. He also contended that the judge wrongly relied on the absence of a democratic election at the meeting to invalidate Aregbesola’s assumption of office under Section 82(3) of the Electoral Act 2022 and Section 223(1)(a) of the 1999 Constitution. According to the lawyer, Section 82(3) governs elections to party governing bodies, including elections to fill vacancies, while Article 23(4) of the ADC constitution empowers the appropriate executive organ to appoint an eligible replacement pending an election at the next convention or congress. “The absence of voting did not resolve whether the resolutions effected an election or an interim appointment under the provision relied upon by the appellant,” he argued. “The lower court applied the requirements governing an election to fill a vacancy without first resolving whether the appellant’s assumption of office fell within the interim appointment power asserted under Article 23(4).” Aregbesola seeks stay of execution In a separate motion on notice filed on Saturday at the Federal High Court, Aregbesola sought a stay of execution of the November 5 judgment pending the hearing and determination of his appeal. The application, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025, seeks an order restraining the enforcement of, or further consequential steps pursuant to, Orders 7 and 8 of the judgment. item.title: Makinde campaign to Tinubu: You weakened Naira, stop claiming credit for recovery
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation has accused President Bola Tinubu of taking credit for the recovery of the naira after presiding over its depreciation through what it described as poorly managed economic reforms. The organisation said Nigerians were yet to recover from the effects of the currency’s depreciation and rising cost of living, insisting that an improved exchange rate meant little while millions struggled to afford food, medication and other basic necessities. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, the organisation described Tinubu’s claim that Nigerians would have needed wheelbarrows to purchase ordinary food items without his intervention as a distortion of the country’s economic experience. “Mr President, you cannot preside over the destruction of the purchasing power of our national currency and turn around to seek public applause,” Ihediwa said. Recalling the exchange rate when Tinubu assumed office on May 29, 2023, the organisation said he inherited an official rate of approximately N461 to the dollar, but his removal of petrol subsidy and unification of foreign exchange windows contributed to the naira’s subsequent depreciation to nearly N2,000 to the dollar. It also faulted the President’s description of an exchange rate of N1,340 to the dollar as ‘pocketable’, arguing that the figure did not reflect the financial reality of ordinary Nigerians. “The real test of economic recovery is whether Nigerians can afford to live better, not simply whether the naira can exchange for more dollars now than when he plunged it into the abyss,” the organisation argued. Questioning the human cost of the economic hardship, Ihediwa asked: “Does President Tinubu have any empathy towards thousands of Nigerians who lost their lives because they could not afford life-saving food and medications under his administration?” The organisation further cited poverty, a $2.3 trillion infrastructure deficit and public debt of N166.7 trillion as evidence of what it described as the administration’s poor economic record. “A President seeking re-election must defend his actual record, not campaign on falsehood and imaginary heroism,” it said. Turning to the 2027 election, the organisation presented the RESET Nigeria Agenda of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde, as an alternative to the Tinubu administration’s economic policies. Anchored on the principles of ‘Stop the Loss, Recover Value and Build Systems That Prevent Failures’, the agenda, according to the organisation, seeks to make citizens’ welfare the measure of economic recovery. “Under the RESET Nigeria Agenda, rising oil revenues must translate into better living conditions, not merely larger government borrowing,” it said. item.title: Lagos 2027: Governorship debate begins in Lekki
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The 2027 Lagos State governorship debate has commenced in Lekki, with key candidates taking the stage to present their programmes and address issues affecting residents of the state. The debate, organised by the Nigeria Debate Consultative, is a collaborative initiative involving Channels Television, TVC News, News Central, Inspiration FM, Cool FM, Vanguard Media and Punch Newspapers. The organisers said the exercise is aimed at promoting credible journalism, democratic accountability and informed electoral choices ahead of the 2027 governorship election. The candidates are expected to present their visions for Lagos State and respond to questions on five key areas: the economy and cost of living; transportation and infrastructure; flooding and the environment; healthcare and social welfare; and security and accountability. Under the debate guidelines, each candidate is allowed three minutes for opening remarks, two minutes to respond to questions and one minute for rebuttals. The candidates are not given prior access to the questions. The participating candidates, selected through what the organisers described as an impartial and transparent survey, are Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour of the African Democratic Congress, ADC; Dr Olufemi Hamzat of the All Progressives Congress, APC; Funsho Doherty of the National Democratic Congress, NDC; and Adedoyin Doherty of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP. Viewers have been encouraged to join the conversation online using the hashtags #LagosGovernorshipDebate, #LagosDecides and #NigeriaDebateConsultative. item.title: LIVE: Hamzat, Rhodes-Vivour, Doherty Face Off As 2027 Elections Debate Series Begins In Lagos
item.description: The Nigeria Debate Consortium, a series of debates for the 2027 general elections in Nigeria, has begun with the Lagos governorship debate. The debate is the first in the series organised by the consortium, which comprises Channels Television, TVC News, Punch Newspaper, The Cable, and Vanguard Newspaper, in selected battleground states ahead of the 2027 elections. The Lagos debate is currently being held at The Hub by IALA, House of His Glory, Plot 18, Providence Road, beside Keystone Bank, Marwa, in the Lekki area of Lagos. Among the major contenders for the Lagos governorship seat are incumbent Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Funso Doherty of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and Deji Doherty of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). The initiative provides a credible, non-partisan platform for participating candidates to present their agendas, defend their policy choices and respond to questions on the issues that matter most to Lagos residents. It also provides an opportunity for voters to put the candidates’ capacity, ideas and priorities — from transportation and infrastructure to security, housing, education, healthcare, job creation and economic growth — under public scrutiny before the February 6, 2027, governorship elections. item.title: 2027: Go to polling units, Zulum charges Borno APC
item.description: … Governor inaugurates campaign council, urges grassroots mobilisation, party unity By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Prof. Babagana Umara Zulum, has charged members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) 2027 Campaign Council to take their mobilisation efforts to wards and polling units across the state to secure increased voter turnout for the party. Zulum, who is chairman of the campaign council, gave the charge on Sunday while inaugurating the council at the Multipurpose Hall of Government House, Maiduguri. He said the party must earn the renewed confidence of voters through service, persuasion and effective organisation, warning members against relying solely on previous electoral victories. “Every member of this Campaign Council must take personal responsibility. Go to your local government area. Go to your ward. Go to your polling unit. Meet the people, listen to them and work with the party structures on the ground,” the governor said. He urged council members to actively involve women and young people in the campaign, engage party elders and submit regular reports on their mobilisation activities. The governor also called for peaceful and lawful campaigns, urging members to educate supporters on the voting process. Addressing disagreements arising from the party’s primaries, Zulum appealed to members who did not secure tickets to remain committed to the party and work collectively towards its success. He also urged successful aspirants to reach out to those who were unsuccessful and address their grievances, warning that actions capable of undermining APC candidates or the party’s collective interests would attract consequences under its constitution. “Our responsibility is to explain this record honestly to the electorate, listen carefully to their concerns and earn their renewed confidence,” he said. Zulum further stressed the need for Borno to deliver increased votes for the APC, noting that the state is the home state of Vice-President Kashim Shettima. He also cited President Bola Tinubu’s support for the establishment of the Federal College of Education in Gwoza, the Federal University of Agriculture and Entrepreneurship in Bama and the National Orthopaedic Hospital in Azare as projects the party intended to highlight during the campaign. The governor expressed confidence in Engr. Mustapha Gubio succeeding him and continuing the work of his administration, urging voters to support APC candidates from the presidential to the state assembly levels. Earlier, the state APC Chairman, Hon. Bello Ayuba, said members of the campaign council were selected based on their experience, political capacity and commitment to the party. He expressed confidence that they would mobilise substantial support for APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. In his goodwill message, the Speaker of the Borno State House of Assembly, Rt. item.title: Train Collision In Egypt’s Giza Kills Four, Injures 88
item.description: Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital on Sunday, derailing several carriages, killing four and injuring dozens, according to the authorities. Egypt’s railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan. The health ministry said an initial count put the toll from the crash at four passengers killed, with 88 others currently being treated for injuries in hospitals around the Giza area. State-owned media had earlier reported 120 people were wounded, without clarifying the degree of injury. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said he was following the accident “with great concern”, and had directed authorities to conduct an urgent investigation to “hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent”. Emergency crews used cranes to remove the wreckage, the authority said. Several carriages lay on their side, AFP journalists at the scene reported. One end of a train had crumpled into a mangle of steel, while the end of the other — spliced open in the impact — had toppled off the tracks into an adjacent farm. First responders and passersby helped lift one of the victims out of the wreckage in a black body bag, AFP images showed. Egyptian rescuers carry the body of a person killed in a train collision in al-Ayyat in Giza governate southern Cairo on November 8, 2026. Photo by – / AFP Authorities said they had launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, which occurred in Giza’s Al-Ayyat area, the site of Egypt’s worst-ever rail disaster. In 2002, more than 370 people were killed when a fire swept through a train carrying holiday travellers south of Cairo. In 2009, multiple train crashes in the area killed dozens. Egypt’s 110 million people depend heavily on rail transport, but the network — one of the largest in Africa — has suffered repeated deadly accidents. Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its ageing rail network. item.title: One dies as truck overturns in Lagos midnight crash
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni One person has died after a fully loaded Mercedes-Benz six-tyre truck overturned around the TREM axis of Gbagada, inward Oshodi, Lagos State, in a midnight accident. The deceased, an elderly man whose identity had yet to be established, was reportedly thrown out of the truck after one of its front tyres burst, causing the driver to lose control of the vehicle. The truck, with registration number ABJ 37 AC, was conveying assorted consignments, including sealed bags and newly branded event chairs, when the incident occurred. According to reports, the vehicle was travelling at considerable speed when the tyre burst. In the ensuing struggle to stabilise the truck, the passenger seated in the front cabin was flung out and hit his head against a sharp object, resulting in his instant death. The Lagos State Traffic Management Authority (LASTMA) said its Night Rescue Team, which was conducting surveillance along major traffic corridors, promptly mobilised to the scene and cordoned off the accident site. The operatives subsequently evacuated the deceased from the busy carriageway into an ambulance operated by the Lagos State Emergency Medical Services (LASEMS), to prevent further exposure to approaching motorists and avert another accident. The General Manager of LASTMA, Mr Olalekan Bakare-Oki, expressed condolences to the family of the deceased, describing the incident as a painful and avoidable loss that underscored the dangers of poor road safety practices. Bakare-Oki said the rescue and traffic management operations received support from personnel of the Pedro Police Division, who provided security, and officers of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, who assisted with emergency response. He explained that the overturned truck could not be immediately recovered because of the volume and nature of its cargo. Arrangements were therefore made to transfer the consignments into another empty truck before recovering the vehicle. The LASTMA boss condemned excessive speeding, warning that it reduces drivers’ reaction time, compromises vehicle stability and increases the severity of road crashes, particularly when unexpected mechanical failures occur. He said the consequences of the accident could have been less severe if the truck had been travelling at a controlled speed, despite the sudden tyre burst. Bakare-Oki urged heavy-duty vehicle operators, commercial transporters and other motorists to adopt responsible driving practices, conduct regular mechanical inspections and pay close attention to the condition of tyres, braking systems and other critical vehicle components before embarking on journeys. He also advised drivers to remain calm and apply appropriate vehicle-control techniques when confronted with sudden mechanical problems, warning that excessive speed could turn a manageable failure into a fatal incident. item.title: Liverpool return to winning ways with 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace
item.description: Florian Wirtz bagged his first Premier League goal this season as Liverpool got back on track with a 3-1 win against lowly Crystal Palace on Sunday. Andoni Iraola’s side erased the bitter taste of successive losses to Arsenal and Fenerbahce with a comfortable victory at Selhurst Park. Alexis Mac Allister put Liverpool ahead late in the first half before Wirtz, whose last league goal came against the same opponents in April, doubled the Reds’ advantage nine minutes into the second half. Alexander Isak netted Liverpool’s third in the 89th minute before Eddie Nketiah scored a stoppage-time penalty for bottom of the table Palace. Liverpool are up to fourth place after their fourth away league win this season. It was a much-needed success for Iraola, who had started to hear some awkward questions about Liverpool’s inconsistent run in his first season in charge after arriving from Bournemouth to replace the sacked Arne Slot. Yeremy Pino went agonisingly close to opening the scoring for Palace in the 18th minute when he curled against the bar. Palace striker Jorgen Strand Larsen had the ball in the back of Alisson Becker’s net in the 33rd minute. But his celebrations were cut short by the offside flag and a subsequent VAR check. Mac Allister made Palace pay for those misses in the 40th minute, nodding home a Dominik Szoboszlai free-kick in clinical fashion. Wirtz increased Liverpool’s advantage in the 54th minute, guiding a low Bradley Barcola cross into the bottom corner. Palace had a huge chance with just under 15 minutes remaining when Pino was denied by Alisson, who then saved from Jefferson Lerma before Nketiah lashed over. Sweden striker Isak put the result beyond doubt in the 89th minute with a deflected close-range strike. Palace earned a penalty after Dario Osorio clashed heads with Milos Kerkez but Nketiah’s goal was no consolation for under-fire Eagles boss Pierre Sage. item.title: Anambra begins reconstruction of failed roads ahead of Christmas
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Contractors handling major road projects in Anambra State have returned to site to reconstruct failed sections of the roads following a directive by the state government ahead of the forthcoming Christmas season. The development followed concerns over the failure of some portions of the roads, including sections that are yet to be officially commissioned. The affected projects include the Amawbia-Agulu-Ekwulobia-Uga dual carriageway, the Agulu-Nnewi dual carriageway and other major roads across the state. The Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure, Okey Ezeobi, had attributed the failures to extreme rainfall and flash flooding rather than the use of substandard construction materials. He, however, directed the contractors to undertake major reconstruction of the affected sections instead of carrying out temporary, spot repairs, in line with Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s emphasis on quality infrastructure delivery. Barely 12 hours after the directive, the contractors reportedly mobilised to their respective sites, with reconstruction work commencing across the state. At the Amawbia end of the dual carriageway, asphalt on one lane had been completely removed, while sand-filling work was ongoing. Similar activities were observed at the Neni section of the Agulu-Nnewi road and along the Nnewi-Ozubulu-Okija dual carriageway. During a visit to some of the project sites at the weekend, officials of the Ministry of Works were seen monitoring the progress of the reconstruction. Ezeobi had earlier dismissed allegations that the road failures resulted from poor construction, insisting that the contractors engaged by the state government were reputable companies capable of undertaking corrective work. “Because of the quality of these contractors, they are able to return to site to effect reconstruction whenever there is any failure and they do this at no cost to the state. “If we had given the contract to small companies, they won’t come back to address the failures. We took time to select all the contractors working for us,” he said. The commissioner attributed the affected portions to the impact of natural disasters, recalling that the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) had earlier issued warnings about possible flooding during the year. He explained that roads located in flood-prone areas were particularly vulnerable, citing sections of the Amawbia-Ekwulobia dual carriageway where swamps and underground water movements had contributed to the damage. “Roads along flood-prone areas in the state are adversely affected. For instance, the Amawbia-Ekwulobia dual carriageway is erosion-prone as there are swamps in some areas and the water there is always struggling to come up. “So in the affected places, we will remove the asphalt and do cement-based stabilisation to help suppress further underground water coming up to destroy it,” he said. item.title: Bauchi police arrest two suspected armed robbers, recover motorcycle
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested two suspected armed robbers and recovered a stolen motorcycle and other valuables following a machete attack on two residents of the state. The suspects, alongside a third accomplice who is still at large, allegedly attacked a 26-year-old man at his residence in the Rafin Makaranta area of Bauchi metropolis in the early hours of November 6, 2026, inflicting machete injuries on his head. The attackers, reportedly armed with machetes, also dispossessed the victim and his friend, a resident of Makera area, of a motorcycle, two mobile phones, Bluetooth devices, power banks, an MP3 player, perfume and N45,000 cash. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Nafiu Habib, disclosed this in a statement issued on Sunday in Bauchi. Habib said operatives attached to the C Division responded to the incident and launched a manhunt for the perpetrators, leading to the arrest of two suspects on November 7. He identified the suspects as Uzairu Rabiu, alias Gwano, of Zawiyya area, Bauchi, and Hafizu Abdullahi, alias Tora, of Gubi village, Bauchi. According to him, the operatives recovered a stolen Haojue motorcycle, two mobile phones and a Bluetooth device from the suspects. The police spokesman added that the injured victim was receiving treatment at the Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital (ATBUTH), Bauchi, and his condition was steadily improving. He said efforts were ongoing to apprehend the third suspect and recover the remaining stolen items. Habib added that the arrested suspects would be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigations. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police, CP Sani-Omolori Aliyu, commended the operatives for their swift response and urged residents to remain vigilant and provide timely and credible information to the police. He warned criminal elements to desist from violent activities, assuring residents that the command would sustain its operations to tackle armed robbery and other criminal activities across the state. item.title: ‎Labour demands immediate start to new Minimum Wage talks
item.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ ‎ABUJA— THE Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) has accused the Federal Government of ignoring the statutory timetable for the next national minimum wage review, insisting that negotiations should already be under way rather than waiting until 2027. ‎ ‎NLC Acting General Secretary, Comrade Benson Upah, speaking to Vanguard in Abuja, said the current N70,000 minimum wage was agreed on July 28, 2024 and backdated to May 1, 2024, but argued that the backdating did not alter the three-year review cycle introduced by the 2024 amendment to the Minimum Wage Act. ‎ ‎“In our estimation, the negotiations ought to have been on the way, or ought to be on the way, because one, the economic realities have since wiped out the value of the ₦70,000, upon which the minimum wage was premised,” Upah said. ‎ ‎He said the 2023 amendment changed only two things: the wage figure, from ₦30,000 to ₦70,000, and the review cycle, from five years to three years, adding that neither change authorised government or labour to shift the commencement date of the three-year cycle at will. ‎ ‎“The principal act was not amended, and there was nothing in the amended items that states that the three yearly cycle can be abridged by either of the parties. ‎ ‎“It is clear that this thing runs on the three yearly cycle now. It is like the constitution says a governor shall hold office for four years, and the governor has to hold office for four years.” ‎ ‎Upah argued that, on the NLC’s reading of the law, the three-year period should be counted from the earlier wage cycle, meaning negotiations ought to have started in June. He said the NLC had already alerted government to that position. ‎ ‎He said: “But if you want to follow the government logic, which is actually an error, that because it took effect from May, that the three years will start from May, if you follow that logic, the negotiations ought to start in November, because the act talks about starting six months before the process. ‎ ‎“So, in our view, there is no reason to do tomorrow what can be done today.” ‎ ‎The NLC scribe said the process of reviewing the minimum wage was lengthy and required hearings, consultations, a cost-of-living assessment and engagement with social partners. ‎ ‎According to him: “It is important for us to start early. Why must we run on a deficit calendar when we knew full well that this thing was going to start on a so-so date? It speaks to our state of unpreparedness.” ‎ ‎His position comes amid an ongoing dispute over when the next review should begin. The Federal Government has maintained that the current N70,000 wage is due for review on June 1, 2027, while organised labour has demanded immediate preparations for a new negotiation. ‎ ‎Asked about suggestions by some labour leaders that the next minimum wage would commence in August 2027, Upah dismissed the claim sharply, saying: “Whichever union leader that made that comment clearly spoke out of ignorance, and acted in erro

item.title: Sunderland beat Chelsea 1-0 to escape Premier League bottom
item.description: Sunderland hauled themselves off the bottom of the Premier League as Enzo Le Fee’s penalty earned a huge 1-0 win over Chelsea for embattled boss Regis Le Bris. The Frenchman was under pressure after a dismal 2-0 home defeat to Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League on Thursday put his position in doubt ahead of an international break. Sunderland, though, bounced back for a huge three points thanks to two controversial penalty decisions. Chelsea were furious that Cole Palmer was not awarded a spot-kick for a foul by Luke O’Nien moments before the only goal of the game. A VAR review deemed the contact made was outside the area and therefore could not be overturned. Sunderland were awarded a penalty at the other end 10 minutes before half-time. The visitors were again aggrieved that Levi Colwill was adjudged to have fouled Brian Brobbey as both players grappled in their attempt to reach the ball. Le Fee dispatched the resulting spot-kick past Mike Penders and Sunderland held on for just a second league win of the season. Chelsea missed the presence of Joao Pedro up front as Palmer and Morgan Rogers were kept in check by the home side. A fourth defeat in 10 league games under Xabi Alonso leaves the Blues in fifth, two points outside the top four. item.title: Flamingos’ Victory Not A Fluke, Performance Reflects Years Of Development – Coach Busari
item.description: Flamingos head coach Hakeem Busari has praised his players for their resilience and tactical discipline after their impressive campaign at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup, while expressing optimism about African football’s future. Busari in a post-match interview, said the performance of African teams at the tournament reflected growing quality, character and competitiveness, despite the challenges posed by strong opposition. The Flamingos became the first African team to win the competition, with goals from Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku securing the historic victory. He noted that the Flamingos had competed in a difficult group that included the defending champions, adding that the experience demonstrated the progress being made in African women’s youth football. “What we are seeing now is not a fluke. It is about development, it is about character, and it is about fighting from the beginning to really get it right. So we are elated and happy,” he said. The coach also expressed hope that more African teams would progress beyond the knockout stages in future editions of the competition and eventually reach the final. Reflecting on the Flamingos’ encounter with Japan, Busari explained that his technical crew had identified the Japanese team’s strength in winning second balls and exploiting spaces behind defensive lines. ﻿ He said the team adjusted its approach to limit Japan’s attacking opportunities, particularly by directing long balls into spaces rather than areas where the opposition could easily gain possession. Busari explained that the Flamingos initially sought to score early before adopting a more cautious approach after taking the lead, but Japan eventually found an equaliser through a set-piece situation. He described the encounter as a tactical contest that required collective defending, discipline and effective game management. According to him, the final stages of the match presented additional challenges as fatigue and anxiety began to affect the young players. Flamingos head coach Hakeem Busari celebrating the victory over Japan in the finals of the U-17 World Cup at Rabat on Saturday “The young girls are tired. We have to manage their mental scenario at that point in time. We have to manage the tactics where they need to just hustle for the ball, play fewer touches and play to the zones where the Japanese are less at home,” he explained. He identified dedication, determination and discipline as key principles that guided the team’s approach. “We need to play to our own strengths, not to the opposition’s strengths. Because if we open the game, they are quicker and they can get more one-v-ones,” he said. The coach added that the Flamingos deliberately pressed Japan to force long balls, which would give them opportunities to recover possession and launch attacks. item.title: Ibom Deep Sea Port: Gov Eno Hails Tinubu’s Approval, Projects Economic Transformation
item.description: Akwa Ibom State Governor, Umo Eno, has described President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s approval of financing arrangements for the Ibom Deep Sea Port as a defining moment in the state’s economic development. He stated this in a statewide broadcast following the President’s visit to Akwa Ibom on Friday, November 6, during which he announced approval for the project. Governor Eno said the deep seaport would serve as a gateway to economic transformation, opening up opportunities in international trade, investment, industrial growth and employment. He expressed confidence that the project would reposition Akwa Ibom as a major economic and maritime hub in Nigeria and the Gulf of Guinea. Governor Eno thanked President Tinubu for his confidence in the state and commitment to national development, assuring him of the Akwa Ibom State Government’s full cooperation towards the successful realisation of the project. ﻿ He described the approval as a significant step in the state’s economic journey and said the government recognised the responsibility that came with the opportunity. The governor also commended residents for their participation in the President’s visit, noting that the reception reflected Akwa Ibom’s reputation as a peaceful, welcoming and investment-ready state. He expressed appreciation to traditional rulers, religious leaders, political stakeholders, youths, women, security agencies, public servants, students and other groups who contributed to the successful hosting of the President. On the forthcoming 2027 general election, he pledged that Akwa Ibom people would support President Tinubu at the polls on January 16, 2027, as part of efforts to ensure continuity in the administration beginning May 29, 2027.
